G-2; The merger agreement, the registration statement, the 8-K filings of 16 June, 18 August and 28 October 2026, and Huntsman's financial statements and debt are not supplied; Source gap, MATERIAL; The quarterly reports and releases describe the merger only in summary; Combined-company leverage, Forward credit model, Business & governance; Supply the merger agreement and Huntsman's latest annual and quarterly statements

G-3; No Q4 2025 earnings release; the FY2025 adjusted EBITDA reconciliation is absent and only the trailing figure of 651.8 at 31 December 2025 appears; Source gap, MINOR; Searched all releases and the annual report for adjusted EBITDA; Financial foundation (Q4 2025 quarter); Derive Q4 2025 from FY2025 less nine months 2025, or supply the February 2026 release

G-4; The proxy statement (board, committees, executive officers, compensation, ownership) and the subsidiary list are not supplied; Source gap, MINOR; The annual report incorporates these items by reference; Business & governance; guarantor identity; Supply the 2026 proxy statement and the list of subsidiaries

G-5; No agency publications, market quotes, peers, portfolio inputs or investor presentation and call slides; the run settings leave these blank; Source gap, MINOR; Run settings and the Q3 release, which refers to slides on the issuer's website; Ratings & triggers, Security selection, Committee decision; Supply them if those modules are requested

G-6; The headline liquidity of about USD 1.3 billion is not itemized; the two builds from printed components give 1,244.4 and 1,278.4; Definition gap, MINOR; Searched all releases and the Q3 report for how liquidity is built; Liquidity; State the build in the Liquidity analysis and label it as a calculation

G-7; The July 2026 quarterly report mentions expense reimbursement of up to USD 30 million besides the termination fee, and the October 2026 report does not; Conflict between periods, MINOR; Compared the two risk-factor passages; Business & governance; Fundamental credit; Treat the termination fee of USD 121 million as the stated figure and flag the reimbursement as not established

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against reading leverage at 7.76x is that reported EBITDA is depressed by an outage and by charges the issuer treats as temporary: higher costs and lost sales at the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer plant cost the chlor alkali and vinyls segment USD 32.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, and the issuer guides fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA to USD 80 million to USD 100 million, above the USD 67.7 million of the fourth quarter of 2025. If that recovery holds and the add-backs stop, trailing adjusted EBITDA would rise from USD 536.6 million and the issuer's 5.2x would be the better measure; if restructuring and litigation charges continue, the reported 7.76x is the better guide, and a covenant relief period that ends no later than 30 September 2027 makes the answer matter. limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The legal ranking, security and guarantor scope of the senior notes, the recovery zone bonds and the receivables financing are not stated in any supplied source, so no debt stack is drawn and structural priority cannot be assessed; severity High; the indentures, the credit agreement and the list of subsidiary guarantors would close it. - Adjusted EBITDA for 2024 is not stated, so adjusted leverage and adjusted cover are not calculable for 31 December 2024; severity Medium; the issuer's fiscal 2024 adjusted EBITDA reconciliation would close it. - The reconciliation of fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA to reported EBITDA is not supplied: only the issuer's trailing figure of USD 651.8 million at 31 December 2025 appears, USD 107.4 million above the calculated reported EBITDA of USD 544.4 million, with no stated bridge; severity Medium; the issuer's fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release would close it. - No fourth-quarter 2025 release was supplied, so fourth-quarter 2025 sales, EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA are calculated as the fiscal year less nine months; severity Medium; the issuer's fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release would close it. - The maturity year of the recovery zone bonds of USD 83.0 million is not stated; the annual report places them after 2030 and the maturity ladder leaves them out, so the ladder principal of USD 2,947.7 million is USD 65.4 million below carrying value; severity Medium; the bond documents would close it. - The issuer's headline liquidity of about USD 1.3 billion is not itemized; the two builds from printed components are USD 1,244.4 million and USD 1,278.4 million, and the charts use the lower, revolver-only build; severity Medium; the issuer's own liquidity definition would close it. - Covenant levels, step-downs and definitions are not stated in any supplied source, so covenant capacity is not calculated; severity Medium; the credit agreement and its amendments would close it. - The letters of credit issued under the revolver at 31 December 2024 are not stated, so undrawn commitments at that date are not supplied; severity Low; the 2024 annual report would close it. - Where a statement prints a dash the table carries not supplied rather than zero: acquisition-related costs before the second quarter of 2026, legacy litigation and environmental recoveries in most periods, several investing and financing lines, additional paid-in capital before 2026 and the noncontrolling-interest line in some periods; severity Low; no action is needed. - Interest expense and interest income are printed separately only in the annual and first-quarter statements; elsewhere the statements print interest expense, net, so the separate lines are not supplied for those columns; severity Low; the net line is complete in every column. - Per-share data and share counts are not carried because their units differ from the statements; severity Low; they are printed in each statement. - Corporate and unallocated segment lines are not carried, so segment results in the income statement table do not sum to income before taxes; severity Low; the corporate lines are printed in each earnings release. - Discrete second-quarter and third-quarter cash flows are not printed because the quarterly reports present year-to-date cash flows; severity Low; they can be derived by subtraction. - Interest rates for the term loan, revolver and recovery zone bonds are stated only at 31 December 2025, and the pricing grid is not supplied; severity Low; the credit agreement would close it.

facts.label: Ownership and control
facts.text: Governance risk comes from board decisions, not from a controlling owner, because Olin is a listed company and the sources name no sponsor, parent or controlling holder. facts.text: The last new debt issue was on 14 March 2025, when Olin entered into a USD 1,850.0 million senior credit facility maturing in March 2030 and issued USD 600.0 million of senior notes due 2033, using the proceeds to redeem the USD 108.6 million notes due 2025 and the USD 500.0 million notes due 2027 and to repay the earlier facility. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The deterioration is an earnings problem rather than a borrowing problem, and most of it sits in chlor alkali. Net debt rose USD 138.6 million in nine months while trailing reported EBITDA fell from USD 544.4 million to USD 360.8 million. Of the USD 190.6 million fall in chlor alkali and vinyls segment results, the Freeport outage at USD 72.2 million and a legacy litigation charge of USD 36.1 million explain 56.8%, and lower volumes, lower prices, higher raw material costs and a smaller hydrogen tax credit explain the rest, partly offset by USD 59.2 million of lower operating costs. Epoxy results improved by USD 98.0 million and Winchester by USD 10.0 million over the same nine months. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation cp2-1; calculation cp2-12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–43

The add-backs total USD 81.7 million in nine months and USD 175.8 million over twelve months. Restructuring recurs, with about USD 70.0 million more expected through 2030, and merger costs of USD 35.0 million to USD 40.0 million are expected for 2026. The Freeport outage cost of USD 72.2 million is not added back, so treating it as non-recurring would lower adjusted leverage to 4.60x. Executive performance shares are now measured on adjusted EBITDA, which is a reason to read that measure with care. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Free cash flow after dividends is close to break-even rather than deeply negative once the litigation payment is set aside. Operating cash flow of USD 69.7 million in nine months was reduced by about USD 114.0 million paid to Shintech; adding it back gives free cash flow of USD 77.1 million before dividends and USD 8.8 million after, against negative USD 105.2 million as reported. Over the last twelve months free cash flow was USD 221.5 million before and USD 130.4 million after dividends, helped by a working-capital inflow of about USD 408.0 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, which lifted that quarter's operating cash flow to USD 321.2 million, and by litigation costs accrued in 2025 and paid in 2026. Nine-month 2026 working capital absorbed USD 191.0 million, so full-year 2026 cash flow again depends on a fourth-quarter release and durable free cash flow is modest at this earnings level. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity gives time but its quality depends on the covenant relief. USD 1,244.4 million of liquidity covers the USD 465.0 million receivables financing due in November 2027 at 2.68x, and 84.2% of the debt principal falls due between 2029 and 2033, so no refinancing is forced in the next twelve months. At the end of 2025 the leverage covenant capped additional borrowing at USD 825.3 million against USD 1,199.6 million of nominal revolver headroom, a gap of USD 374.3 million, and the relief under which no covenant limited borrowing at 30 September 2026 ends by 30 September 2027 at the latest. The covenant levels after relief are not stated, so headroom after relief cannot be calculated. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Diversification is average and margin stability weak, because three segments rest on one cyclical chlor alkali base and one site. Chlor alkali and vinyls is 54% of sales and its nine-month sales fell 14.2% on lower volumes and prices, Freeport hosts 9 of the 10 chemical product lines, and combined segment results fell 83.7% from 2023 to 2025 while sales slipped 0.8%. Pricing power is limited: Winchester's higher prices of USD 44.1 million were outrun by USD 57.3 million of higher raw material and operating costs, and epoxy still competes with subsidised Asian imports. Contracted backlog and military demand give Winchester visibility. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a cautious view is that earnings are near a trough set partly by events that may not recur. The outage cost USD 72.2 million of nine-month results and is not added back even in the issuer's 5.2x, treating it as non-recurring gives 4.60x, fourth-quarter guidance points to between 4.92x and 5.10x, Fitch has Olin on positive watch, no debt matures before November 2027 and the Winchester backlog stands at USD 1,331 million. Cost actions are also real, with USD 118.7 million of lower operating costs in chlor alkali and epoxy over nine months. The view would turn more positive if the merger documents show combined leverage below Olin's own and unchanged ranking for the notes, or if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA exceeds USD 100 million; it would turn more negative if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA falls below USD 80 million, if closing slips beyond the first quarter of 2027, or if covenant relief ends before earnings recover. The monitoring triggers set out these signals. facts.text: The strongest credit support is time and liquidity: USD 1,244.4 million of liquidity, no maturity before the USD 465.0 million receivables financing in November 2027, and 84.2% of debt principal due between 2029 and 2033. Management has also cut discretionary cash, since buybacks have stopped and nine-month capital spending is 34.8% below the prior year, and the integrated cost base still delivered USD 118.7 million of lower operating costs in chlor alkali and epoxy. Finally, no sponsor or controlling holder is identified, so no owner is extracting value from the group. facts.text: The main weakness is leverage and cover: net debt is 7.76x trailing reported EBITDA and cash interest cover is 2.12x. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Olin is a vertically integrated chemicals and ammunition group. Chlor alkali and vinyls produces 54% of sales from chlorine, caustic soda, vinyls and chlorinated organics, epoxy 20%, and Winchester 26%, including the Lake City plant it operates for the US Army. Cash generation rests on commodity chlor alkali spreads, on epoxy margins that were negative from 2023 to 2025, and on government and commercial ammunition demand. The model supports debt service only when chlor alkali earns a normal margin, because that segment funds most of the group's fixed charges, and it weakens refinancing confidence because 9 of the 10 chemical product lines sit at one site. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation cp2-10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–9

facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Olin Corporation is a listed Virginia company with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so financial policy is set by a board answerable to dispersed holders. The bank facility is guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries and secured by liens until the relief period ends, which puts bank debt ahead of unsecured creditors for now, and the guarantees and ranking of the notes are not stated. The Huntsman merger would give existing Olin shareholders about 54.5% of the combined company, and the creditor effect depends on documents that were not supplied. Distributions above the regular dividend are limited during the relief period and the buyback authorization of USD 1,948.9 million is unused. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Chlor alkali revenue is cyclical and price-taking: nine-month sales fell on lower volumes, mainly the wound-down Blue Water Alliance trading, and lower prices, with chlorine sold in substantial quantities to a relatively small number of industrial users and no customer above 10% of group sales. Epoxy sales rose on higher volumes and prices but face subsidised Asian imports, so the gain is not yet shown to be durable. Winchester revenue is the most predictable because of its backlog and military contracts, yet its price increases were outrun by metal and propellant costs. Revenue is therefore cyclical in chemicals and contracted in ammunition, and the first is the larger and the more exposed to substitution by imports. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: The cost base is energy-linked and largely fixed. Electricity is the largest raw material and about 76% of it comes from natural gas or hydroelectric sources, raw material and utility purchase commitments total USD 5,559.4 million with 13.0% due within a year, and depreciation and amortization was USD 521.6 million in 2025. Operating cost actions delivered USD 118.7 million of savings in chlor alkali and epoxy over nine months, but raw material costs rose by USD 32.1 million in chlor alkali and USD 33.1 million in epoxy, so margins can be defended through cost actions rather than pricing. Chlor alkali gross margin fell to 9.5% from 14.0% in nine months, and restructuring will continue, with about USD 70.0 million of further charges expected through 2030. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Rivalry is the force that matters most: Olin competes with large chlor alkali producers in North America and, in epoxy, with Huntsman, Westlake and Asian producers, and subsidised Asian exports are cited by management as a pressure on the fourth quarter, which transmits into lower prices and margins. New entrants are a weak force because plants need large capital investment and permits. Buyers are moderately strong: chlorine goes to a small number of industrial users and Winchester sells to retailers and governments. Suppliers matter for Winchester, which buys propellant mainly from one large supplier and metals at exchange-linked prices, and for energy, which is the largest raw material. Substitutes for chlorine and caustic soda are not established from the sources. facts.label: Political, economic and regulatory factors
facts.text: Regulatory and economic factors are material and social and technological factors are not. Environmental obligations carry a reserve of USD 156.8 million and expected expense of USD 25 million to USD 30 million in 2026, the State of Texas has sued over emissions at Freeport, and the clean hydrogen production tax credit that benefited chlor alkali results is smaller in 2026, with the annual pretax benefit expected at USD 15 million to USD 20 million to 2028. Trade policy is fluid after the 20 February 2026 Supreme Court ruling on emergency tariffs, Winchester reports partly tariff-driven metal inflation, and Middle East conflict has raised feedstock and energy costs, though the issuer reports no significant direct effect. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The downside begins with a second operating shock at Freeport or a prolonged weak chlor alkali price on top of year-end destocking. The first operational break is the vinyl chloride monomer plant running at reduced rates, as in the second quarter of 2026, when the issuer said the disruption reduced adjusted EBITDA by USD 40.0 million. That lowers trailing reported EBITDA to USD 320.8 million, lifts net leverage to 8.72x and cuts interest cover to 1.88x, and a failed merger with the USD 121 million termination fee would lift leverage to 9.10x on unchanged cash. Liquidity of USD 1,244.4 million still covers the USD 465.0 million receivables financing, so distress within a year is not indicated, but the covenant relief, under which no covenant limited borrowing at 30 September 2026, ends by 30 September 2027 and headroom after it is not calculable. Management can cut capital spending, guided at about USD 200.0 million for 2026, and the quarterly dividend of about USD 22.7 million, while asset sales are limited during relief. Observable triggers are fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA below USD 80 million and any slip in merger closing. facts.text: Overall, Olin presents a not fully assessable business profile supported by liquidity, a long maturity profile, improving epoxy and Winchester results and the absence of a sponsor, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 7.76x on reported EBITDA, thin free cash flow and concentration in chlor alkali at one site. Cash-flow durability appears weak at this earnings level because free cash flow after dividends is near break-even, depends on a fourth-quarter working-capital release and sits beside recurring add-backs. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on fourth-quarter earnings, the end of covenant relief by 30 September 2027, the receivables financing due in November 2027 and the merger terms. The primary downside path is a second outage or weak chlor alkali prices meeting the end of covenant relief before earnings recover. Further analysis would require the covenant levels, the merger agreement, Huntsman's statements and peer data, and the business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established. # CP-0 Source readiness: OLIN Corp (oln)
## Request

OLIN Corp (oln), as of 2026-11-05: source readiness for the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot) over the seven supplied filings and earnings releases. The run asks for Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit; this module maps content to them, records gaps and states no credit view.
## Sources

No output from an earlier module was supplied to this module; it is the entry module of the run.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases support a snapshot of Olin's consolidated position to 30 September 2026, but not the covenant, financing-document or post-merger questions that decide creditor protection. The statements, the debt note, facility availability and the issuer-reported agency ratings are complete to that date, while covenant levels, the indentures and credit agreement, the merger agreement and Huntsman's own financials are absent.

Reported net debt of USD 2,798.3 million and net leverage of 5.2x trace to the filings and recompute exactly. Covenant headroom and the combined company's leverage cannot be established from these sources, so any later conclusion on them must be marked as a gap.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–15; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation cp0-2; calculation cp0-5
### Key findings

The sources cover the 2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports and the three matching earnings releases, dated from 20 February 2026 to 30 October 2026, so nothing in them postdates the 5 November 2026 as-of date. The fourth quarter of 2025 is not reported separately and has to be derived from the annual figures less the first nine months of 2025.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 150; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, page 1

The reporting entity is Olin Corporation, a Virginia company that reports consolidated statements for itself and its subsidiaries, so those statements are the issuer's own figures for debt, earnings, leverage and coverage; the sources hold no separate statements for a borrowing or finance subsidiary. Certain domestic subsidiaries guarantee the senior secured credit facility, but the sources do not name them.

The September 2026 debt note lists every instrument: three series of senior notes, the term loan, the revolver, the receivables financing and the recovery zone bonds, which total USD 3,013.1 million after deducting USD 17.6 million of deferred issuance costs. With cash of USD 214.8 million this gives net debt of USD 2,798.3 million. Undrawn revolver commitments are USD 1,029.6 million and receivables headroom is USD 34.0 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 12, 13, 15; calculation cp0-1; calculation cp0-2; calculation cp0-6

The ratings table in the annual report is dated 19 February 2026 and is superseded: at 30 September 2026 Fitch rates Olin BB+ on Rating Watch Positive, Moody's rates it Ba2 with a negative outlook and S&P rates it BB on Credit Watch Developing. These are Olin's own statements, and no agency report was supplied.

The Huntsman merger is known only through Olin's own summaries. Closing is now expected in the first quarter of 2027, against the first half of 2027 in the July 2026 quarterly report; shareholders approved the transaction on 25 August 2026 and the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period has expired. Olin could owe a termination fee of USD 121 million, and the July report also mentioned expense reimbursement of up to USD 30 million that the October report does not repeat.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_oln-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 58; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, page 1

The senior secured credit facility carries a maximum net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio, relaxed by an amendment of 19 February 2026 for a relief period that ends on the earlier of 30 September 2027 or Olin's election. No source prints the covenant levels, step-downs or definitions, or the issuer's reported covenant ratio, so headroom is not established; Olin states that it was in compliance at 30 September 2026.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against calling these sources sufficient is that two questions a creditor needs answered after the 2026 downgrades, how much covenant headroom remains and what the merged group's leverage will be, cannot be answered from them. The readiness view would change for Fundamental credit, and for Legal & covenants if it were requested, if the credit agreement's covenant levels, Huntsman's financial statements or the merger agreement's financing terms were supplied.
### Limitations
Page references in this run follow the numbered text records of each supplied file, not the printed page numbers of the filings.
Agency ratings, merger terms and credit facility terms are Olin's own descriptions; the agency reports, the merger agreement and the credit agreement were not read.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Olin's net debt of USD 2,798.3 million is 7.76x trailing reported EBITDA, up from 4.89x at the end of 2025, and only the issuer's own add-backs bring it down to 5.2x, so creditor protection rests on those add-backs being non-recurring. Net debt rose USD 138.6 million in nine months while trailing reported EBITDA fell from USD 544.4 million to USD 360.8 million, so the deterioration comes from earnings, not from borrowing.

Reported EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.12x, and nine-month operating cash flow of USD 69.7 million funded neither capital spending of USD 106.6 million nor dividends of USD 68.3 million; net borrowings of USD 185.3 million covered the gap. Liquidity of USD 1,244.4 million and no maturity before November 2027 give time.

### Key findings
#### Leverage trajectory and drivers

Net debt to trailing reported EBITDA rose from 3.17x at the end of 2024 to 4.89x at the end of 2025 and 7.76x at 30 September 2026, and total debt to EBITDA reached 8.35x. Net debt was USD 2,666.6 million, USD 2,659.7 million and USD 2,798.3 million on those dates, so the ratio moved with earnings: reported EBITDA fell from USD 840.6 million in 2024 to USD 544.4 million in 2025 and to USD 360.8 million for the twelve months to September 2026. The issuer's adjusted measure gives 4.1x at the end of 2025 and 5.2x at September 2026; the reported measure leads here because the add-backs are not shown to be non-recurring.

Basis: calculation cp1-1; calculation cp1-2; calculation cp1-5; calculation cp1-7; calculation cp1-8; calculation cp1-9; calculation cp1-14; calculation cp1-15; calculation cp1-16; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, page 11

The gap between the two measures is USD 175.8 million over the last twelve months and USD 81.7 million in the first nine months of 2026, which comprises restructuring charges of USD 21.3 million, legacy litigation of USD 36.1 million and merger-related costs of USD 24.3 million. Restructuring has been charged in every period presented, so it behaves as a running cost rather than a one-off, and the fiscal 2025 reconciliation that would show what was added back in the fourth quarter is not supplied.
Basis: calculation cp1-19; calculation cp1-28; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 81
#### Coverage

Cash interest paid was USD 170.2 million over the last twelve months, so reported EBITDA covers it 2.12x, down from 4.65x in 2024 and 3.06x in 2025; on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the cover is 3.15x. Interest expense, net was USD 130.9 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 138.1 million a year earlier, so cover is falling because earnings fall, not because the cost of debt rises.
Basis: calculation cp1-11; calculation cp1-17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5
#### Cash-flow quality

Operating cash flow was USD 69.7 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 153.0 million a year earlier. After capital spending of USD 106.6 million, free cash flow was negative USD 36.9 million, and after dividends of USD 68.3 million the shortfall was USD 105.2 million; net borrowings of USD 185.3 million funded it and cash rose USD 47.2 million. Receivables absorbed USD 133.4 million of cash.
Basis: calculation cp1-20; calculation cp1-21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5
#### Liquidity and maturities

Liquidity at 30 September 2026 was USD 1,244.4 million: cash of USD 214.8 million plus undrawn revolver commitments of USD 1,029.6 million. Receivables financing headroom of USD 34.0 million is additional but limited by the borrowing base. No debt matures before the USD 465.0 million receivables financing in November 2027; the next maturities are USD 669.3 million in 2029, USD 1,213.4 million in 2030 and USD 600.0 million in 2033, and the recovery zone bonds of USD 83.0 million have no stated maturity year.
Basis: calculation cp1-22; calculation cp1-24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–15
#### Debt composition

Total debt of USD 3,013.1 million is carrying value after USD 17.6 million of deferred issuance costs, against instrument principal of USD 3,030.7 million. Of that principal, USD 1,246.1 million is at variable rates, and the issuer estimates that a 100 bp rise in the reference rate adds USD 12.5 million to annual interest expense. Operating lease liabilities and the accrued pension liability, together USD 584.3 million, sit outside net debt.
Basis: calculation cp1-25; calculation cp1-27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 12, 54
#### Segment drivers and outlook

Third-quarter 2026 sales were USD 1,747.7 million against USD 1,713.2 million a year earlier, but chlor alkali and vinyls segment results fell to USD 71.3 million from USD 127.6 million. Epoxy earned USD 0.6 million against a loss of USD 32.2 million, and Winchester earned USD 33.8 million against USD 19.3 million. The issuer expects fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA of USD 80 million to USD 100 million, against USD 67.7 million calculated for the fourth quarter of 2025.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8; calculation cp1-13
#### Data quality and subsequent events

Gross debt, cash and net debt agree between the quarterly reports and the issuer's releases at each 2026 quarter end and at 31 December 2025. The issuer's headline liquidity of about USD 1.3 billion is not itemized, and neither a fiscal 2025 reconciliation nor a fourth-quarter 2025 release was supplied, so fourth-quarter 2025 sales of USD 1,665.1 million and EBITDA are calculated. On 27 October 2026 Olin signed a second amendment to its credit facility that provides a senior secured facility of USD 2,500.0 million only if the Huntsman merger closes; it changes no net debt today and is not reflected in any figure here.
Basis: calculation cp1-13; calculation cp1-22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, page 3
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against reading leverage at 7.76x is that reported EBITDA is depressed by an outage and by charges the issuer treats as temporary: higher costs and lost sales at the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer plant cost the chlor alkali and vinyls segment USD 32.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, and the issuer guides fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA to USD 80 million to USD 100 million, above the USD 67.7 million of the fourth quarter of 2025. If that recovery holds and the add-backs stop, trailing adjusted EBITDA would rise from USD 536.6 million and the issuer's 5.2x would be the better measure; if restructuring and litigation charges continue, the reported 7.76x is the better guide, and a covenant relief period that ends no later than 30 September 2027 makes the answer matter.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation cp1-19; calculation cp1-13
### Limitations

Fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024 EBITDA and the fourth quarter of 2025 are calculated from statements and nine-month figures because no fiscal-year reconciliation or fourth-quarter release was supplied; interim denominators are last-twelve-month constructions from year-to-date statements.
Basis: calculation cp1-7; calculation cp1-8; calculation cp1-13; calculation cp1-9

No source states the legal ranking or security of the senior notes or the guarantor names, so no debt stack is drawn and structural priority is not assessed; covenant levels are not stated, so no headroom is calculated.

# CP-1A Business & governance: OLIN Corp (oln)
## Request

OLIN Corp (oln), as of 2026-11-05: Business & governance for the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot) from the seven supplied filings and earnings releases. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, governance, capital allocation and the pending Huntsman merger and its financing. It states no view on ratings, recovery or instrument selection.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Olin is widely held with no controlling shareholder or sponsor in the sources, so creditor risk centres on the pending Huntsman merger, which would put a larger secured bank facility over the combined company before the treatment of existing notes is known.

Sales were almost flat at USD 6,833.0 million in 2023 and USD 6,780.8 million in 2025, but combined segment results fell to USD 145.3 million from USD 888.8 million, and to USD 171.0 million in the first nine months of 2026 from USD 253.6 million. Dividends took 98.0% of nine-month operating cash flow, although buybacks have stopped.

Basis: calculation cp1a-3; calculation cp1a-11; 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 129–131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34
### Key findings
#### Ownership and control

Governance risk comes from board decisions, not from a controlling owner, because Olin is a listed company and the sources name no sponsor, parent or controlling holder. The annual report shows a Chairman separate from the chief executive and nine directors who signed it, but the proxy statement that would list holders of 5% or more, board independence and related-party dealings was not supplied, so dispersed ownership is an inference from the absence of any disclosed controlling holder. No sponsor fees or fund-life pressure arise from this ownership, and the sources supplied disclose no related-party payments.
#### The Huntsman merger and its financing

The merger decides creditor outcomes, and its financing runs through secured bank debt. The all-stock merger of equals would leave existing Olin shareholders with 54.5% of the combined company and Huntsman stockholders with 45.5%, both groups approved it on 25 August 2026, and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027. At closing a new USD 2,500.0 million senior secured facility would replace Olin's term loan of USD 650.0 million and revolver of USD 1,200.0 million, USD 650.0 million more than Olin's own commitments, and would also replace Huntsman's revolver, whose size is not stated. Certain subsidiaries of both companies would guarantee it and it would carry first-priority liens on certain assets. The sources do not say what happens to Olin's existing senior notes or receivables financing, or what Huntsman owes, so the effect on unsecured creditors and the combined leverage are not established.
Basis: calculation cp1a-9; calculation cp1a-10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34
#### Cost and constraints while the merger is pending

A failed or delayed merger has a price, and the pending deal narrows the board's room to act. Olin could owe a termination fee of USD 121 million if the agreement ends under specified circumstances, it booked USD 24.3 million of advisory and legal costs in the first nine months of 2026, shareholder lawsuits about the merger have been filed, and the agreement bars certain actions without Huntsman's consent before closing. These constraints limit how freely management can change financing or capital returns before closing; their exact scope is not stated.
Basis: calculation cp1a-18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58–59
#### Lenders hold security until the relief period ends

Bank lenders took security and payout limits in return for looser covenants in February 2026. The amendment of 19 February 2026 reduced the minimum interest coverage ratio, raised the maximum net leverage ratio and adjusted the EBITDA and debt definitions for a relief period, and at the same time required guarantees from certain material domestic subsidiaries and liens over substantially all of their and Olin's personal property. During the relief period it also limits new debt, certain asset sales and dividends or distributions above the regular dividend, and Olin prepaid part of the term loan with USD 109.7 million of revolver borrowings. The guarantees and liens are released at the latest on 30 September 2027 or earlier if Olin elects, so the banks hold security until then. The covenant levels are not stated, and the sources do not state the guarantees or security of the senior notes, so the position of noteholders is not established.
#### Shareholder returns are cut but still a call on cash

Distributions have fallen sharply but remain a call on thin cash flow. Dividends and buybacks together fell from USD 812.3 million in 2023 to USD 142.1 million in 2025 and USD 68.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, because buybacks stopped after November 2025 while the USD 0.20 quarterly dividend per share, unchanged for five years, continued. In the nine months operating cash flow of USD 69.7 million did not cover capital spending of USD 106.6 million, free cash flow was negative USD 36.9 million before dividends, and net borrowings of USD 185.3 million covered the gap. Management still expects about USD 200 million of capital spending for 2026, which implies about USD 93.4 million in the fourth quarter. A repurchase authorization of USD 1,948.9 million remains open but unused, and while the relief period lasts the credit agreement limits distributions above the regular dividend, so buybacks are constrained and the regular dividend is allowed.

#### Earnings have fallen much faster than sales

The group earns far less on stable sales: combined segment results fell 83.7% from 2023 to 2025 while sales slipped 0.8%. Chlor alkali and vinyls, 54% of 2025 sales, saw results fall from USD 664.2 million to USD 181.1 million, epoxy lost money in each of the three years, and Winchester's results fell from USD 255.6 million to USD 67.7 million, with commercial ammunition sales down 23.9% in 2025 while military and law enforcement sales rose. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against this cautious reading is that the merger could strengthen creditors rather than dilute them. It is an all-stock combination with no cash paid to shareholders, both shareholder groups approved it, the US antitrust waiting period has expired, the bank group has committed a USD 2,500.0 million facility, and the agencies are split, with Fitch on positive watch, S&P on developing watch and Moody's holding a negative outlook. The recovery of epoxy and Winchester earnings in 2026 and a backlog of USD 1,331 million also show the diversification working. The view would turn more positive if Huntsman's statements, the merger agreement and the new facility's covenants show lower combined leverage and keep the ranking of existing notes; it would turn negative if closing slips beyond the first quarter of 2027, the USD 121 million termination fee becomes payable, the Lake City labour agreement is not renewed, or chlor alkali results keep falling.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On 15 June 2026 Olin entered into a definitive all-stock merger agreement with Huntsman Corporation to form OlinHuntsman Corporation, announced the next day. Each Huntsman share converts into a fixed number of Olin shares, which leaves existing Olin shareholders with about 54.5% and Huntsman stockholders with about 45.5% of the combined company. The shareholders of both companies approved on 25 August 2026, the registration statement was declared effective on 13 July 2026, the US antitrust waiting period has expired, closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027 subject to remaining regulatory approvals, and Olin could owe a termination fee of USD 121 million if the agreement ends in specified circumstances. Acquisition-related costs were USD 24.3 million in the first nine months of 2026.

Basis: calculation cp1a-10; calculation cp1a-18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, page 3

The financing for the merger is a second amendment, signed on 27 October 2026, to Olin's credit agreement. On the closing date it would provide a USD 2,500.0 million senior secured facility made up of a USD 750.0 million term loan, expected to be fully drawn and replacing Olin's USD 650.0 million term loan, and a USD 1,750.0 million revolver replacing Olin's USD 1,200.0 million revolver and Huntsman's existing revolver. The term loan amortizes quarterly at a higher rate after the fourth anniversary of closing, the facility matures five years after closing, certain subsidiaries of both companies guarantee it, and first-priority liens cover certain assets. The proceeds would refinance the existing bank facility, repay and terminate Huntsman's revolver and pay fees. The covenants restrict the ratio of secured debt to earnings and the interest coverage ratio, and their levels are not stated. The sources do not say what happens to the existing senior notes or the receivables financing.

The last new debt issue was on 14 March 2025, when Olin entered into a USD 1,850.0 million senior credit facility maturing in March 2030 and issued USD 600.0 million of senior notes due 2033, using the proceeds to redeem the USD 108.6 million notes due 2025 and the USD 500.0 million notes due 2027 and to repay the earlier facility. On 19 February 2026 Olin amended that facility to loosen covenants, add guarantees and collateral and prepay term loan amortization with USD 109.7 million of revolver borrowings. No new notes were issued in the first nine months of 2026, and the other transactions in the period were small: a USD 55.8 million cash purchase of ammunition assets in April 2025 and a USD 31.3 million distribution to the noncontrolling holder of the Blue Water Alliance venture in the first quarter of 2026.

# CP-2 Fundamental credit: OLIN Corp (oln)
## Request

OLIN Corp (oln), as of 2026-11-05: Fundamental credit for the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot) from the seven supplied filings and earnings releases and the three earlier module outputs. Scope is business risk, financial profile, outlook, downside, materiality and monitoring; it assigns no rating and makes no security, legal-capacity or sizing recommendation.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Olin is a liquid but deteriorating credit: leverage of 7.76x on reported EBITDA, or 5.2x on the issuer's adjusted measure, and interest cover of 2.12x are held up by USD 1,244.4 million of liquidity and no maturity before November 2027.

That time is the creditor's main protection, and three events in the next twelve months decide whether it is enough: covenant relief ends by 30 September 2027, the receivables financing of USD 465.0 million falls due in November 2027, and the Huntsman merger would replace the bank facility without stating how the notes are treated. Management guides fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA to USD 80 million to USD 100 million, which would put adjusted leverage between 4.92x and 5.10x if net debt is unchanged.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation cp2-1; calculation cp2-3; calculation cp2-8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Key findings

The deterioration is an earnings problem rather than a borrowing problem, and most of it sits in chlor alkali. Net debt rose USD 138.6 million in nine months while trailing reported EBITDA fell from USD 544.4 million to USD 360.8 million. Of the USD 190.6 million fall in chlor alkali and vinyls segment results, the Freeport outage at USD 72.2 million and a legacy litigation charge of USD 36.1 million explain 56.8%, and lower volumes, lower prices, higher raw material costs and a smaller hydrogen tax credit explain the rest, partly offset by USD 59.2 million of lower operating costs. Epoxy results improved by USD 98.0 million and Winchester by USD 10.0 million over the same nine months.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation cp2-1; calculation cp2-12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–43

Reported EBITDA is the safer base for leverage, yet even the issuer's adjusted measure bears the outage, so the run-rate lies between the two. The add-backs total USD 81.7 million in nine months and USD 175.8 million over twelve months. Restructuring recurs, with about USD 70.0 million more expected through 2030, and merger costs of USD 35.0 million to USD 40.0 million are expected for 2026. The Freeport outage cost of USD 72.2 million is not added back, so treating it as non-recurring would lower adjusted leverage to 4.60x. Executive performance shares are now measured on adjusted EBITDA, which is a reason to read that measure with care.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation cp2-2; calculation cp2-4; calculation cp2-16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 141

Free cash flow after dividends is close to break-even rather than deeply negative once the litigation payment is set aside. Operating cash flow of USD 69.7 million in nine months was reduced by about USD 114.0 million paid to Shintech; adding it back gives free cash flow of USD 77.1 million before dividends and USD 8.8 million after, against negative USD 105.2 million as reported. Over the last twelve months free cash flow was USD 221.5 million before and USD 130.4 million after dividends, helped by a working-capital inflow of about USD 408.0 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, which lifted that quarter's operating cash flow to USD 321.2 million, and by litigation costs accrued in 2025 and paid in 2026. Nine-month 2026 working capital absorbed USD 191.0 million, so full-year 2026 cash flow again depends on a fourth-quarter release and durable free cash flow is modest at this earnings level.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation cp2-5; calculation cp2-6; calculation cp2-7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82

Liquidity gives time but its quality depends on the covenant relief. USD 1,244.4 million of liquidity covers the USD 465.0 million receivables financing due in November 2027 at 2.68x, and 84.2% of the debt principal falls due between 2029 and 2033, so no refinancing is forced in the next twelve months. At the end of 2025 the leverage covenant capped additional borrowing at USD 825.3 million against USD 1,199.6 million of nominal revolver headroom, a gap of USD 374.3 million, and the relief under which no covenant limited borrowing at 30 September 2026 ends by 30 September 2027 at the latest. The covenant levels after relief are not stated, so headroom after relief cannot be calculated.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation cp2-8; calculation cp2-9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 140–141

Diversification is average and margin stability weak, because three segments rest on one cyclical chlor alkali base and one site. Chlor alkali and vinyls is 54% of sales and its nine-month sales fell 14.2% on lower volumes and prices, Freeport hosts 9 of the 10 chemical product lines, and combined segment results fell 83.7% from 2023 to 2025 while sales slipped 0.8%. Pricing power is limited: Winchester's higher prices of USD 44.1 million were outrun by USD 57.3 million of higher raw material and operating costs, and epoxy still competes with subsidised Asian imports. Contracted backlog and military demand give Winchester visibility.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation cp2-10; calculation cp2-11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–43

Access to capital markets is average and untested at current leverage. Olin last issued bonds in March 2025, when trailing reported EBITDA was higher and net leverage at the end of 2024 was 3.17x, and the agencies are split, with Fitch on positive watch, S&P on developing watch and Moody's holding a negative outlook. Total debt is 63.7% of total capitalization against 60.2% at the end of 2025, and variable-rate debt is 41.1% of principal, so each 100 bp rise in the reference rate adds USD 12.5 million to annual interest.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation cp2-13; calculation cp2-14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54

Governance and financial policy are average: there is no sponsor to extract value and buybacks have stopped, but the USD 0.20 quarterly dividend continues while free cash flow is negative and the covenant relief limits other distributions. The merger agreement restricts certain actions before closing, and the treatment of the notes at closing is not stated, so policy after the merger is not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 140–141; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59

The outlook is for a weaker fourth quarter and a recovery that depends on chlor alkali. Management expects chemicals and Winchester results to fall from the third quarter on year-end destocking, higher feedstock costs, subsidised Asian exports, planned turnarounds and higher metal costs, with fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 80 million to USD 100 million against USD 191.4 million in the third quarter. That range is above the USD 67.7 million of the fourth quarter of 2025 and would lift trailing adjusted EBITDA from USD 536.6 million to between USD 548.9 million and USD 568.9 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation cp2-3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2

The primary downside path starts at Freeport or in chlor alkali pricing and ends at the 2027 refinancing window. A further outage of the size of the second-quarter hit, USD 40.0 million, would cut trailing reported EBITDA to USD 320.8 million, lift net leverage to 8.72x and cut cash interest cover to 1.88x, and a failed merger with the termination fee of USD 121 million would take leverage to 9.10x on unchanged cash. That would arrive as covenant relief ends and the receivables financing of USD 465.0 million falls due, when headroom under the original covenants is not stated and the merger facility may not exist.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation cp2-15; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_exhibit991q22026earningspr.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a cautious view is that earnings are near a trough set partly by events that may not recur. The outage cost USD 72.2 million of nine-month results and is not added back even in the issuer's 5.2x, treating it as non-recurring gives 4.60x, fourth-quarter guidance points to between 4.92x and 5.10x, Fitch has Olin on positive watch, no debt matures before November 2027 and the Winchester backlog stands at USD 1,331 million. Cost actions are also real, with USD 118.7 million of lower operating costs in chlor alkali and epoxy over nine months. The view would turn more positive if the merger documents show combined leverage below Olin's own and unchanged ranking for the notes, or if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA exceeds USD 100 million; it would turn more negative if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA falls below USD 80 million, if closing slips beyond the first quarter of 2027, or if covenant relief ends before earnings recover. The monitoring triggers set out these signals.

### Strengths and weaknesses

The strongest credit support is time and liquidity: USD 1,244.4 million of liquidity, no maturity before the USD 465.0 million receivables financing in November 2027, and 84.2% of debt principal due between 2029 and 2033. Next, two segments are improving, with epoxy results up USD 98.0 million in nine months and Winchester carrying a backlog of USD 1,331 million. Management has also cut discretionary cash, since buybacks have stopped and nine-month capital spending is 34.8% below the prior year, and the integrated cost base still delivered USD 118.7 million of lower operating costs in chlor alkali and epoxy. Finally, no sponsor or controlling holder is identified, so no owner is extracting value from the group.

### Company description

Olin is a vertically integrated chemicals and ammunition group. Chlor alkali and vinyls produces 54% of sales from chlorine, caustic soda, vinyls and chlorinated organics, epoxy 20%, and Winchester 26%, including the Lake City plant it operates for the US Army. Cash generation rests on commodity chlor alkali spreads, on epoxy margins that were negative from 2023 to 2025, and on government and commercial ammunition demand. The model supports debt service only when chlor alkali earns a normal margin, because that segment funds most of the group's fixed charges, and it weakens refinancing confidence because 9 of the 10 chemical product lines sit at one site.

### Ownership and group structure

Olin Corporation is a listed Virginia company with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so financial policy is set by a board answerable to dispersed holders. The bank facility is guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries and secured by liens until the relief period ends, which puts bank debt ahead of unsecured creditors for now, and the guarantees and ranking of the notes are not stated. The Huntsman merger would give existing Olin shareholders about 54.5% of the combined company, and the creditor effect depends on documents that were not supplied. Distributions above the regular dividend are limited during the relief period and the buyback authorization of USD 1,948.9 million is unused.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 140–141; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Chlor alkali revenue is cyclical and price-taking: nine-month sales fell on lower volumes, mainly the wound-down Blue Water Alliance trading, and lower prices, with chlorine sold in substantial quantities to a relatively small number of industrial users and no customer above 10% of group sales. Epoxy sales rose on higher volumes and prices but face subsidised Asian imports, so the gain is not yet shown to be durable. Winchester revenue is the most predictable because of its backlog and military contracts, yet its price increases were outrun by metal and propellant costs. Revenue is therefore cyclical in chemicals and contracted in ammunition, and the first is the larger and the more exposed to substitution by imports.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

The cost base is energy-linked and largely fixed. Electricity is the largest raw material and about 76% of it comes from natural gas or hydroelectric sources, raw material and utility purchase commitments total USD 5,559.4 million with 13.0% due within a year, and depreciation and amortization was USD 521.6 million in 2025. Operating cost actions delivered USD 118.7 million of savings in chlor alkali and epoxy over nine months, but raw material costs rose by USD 32.1 million in chlor alkali and USD 33.1 million in epoxy, so margins can be defended through cost actions rather than pricing. Chlor alkali gross margin fell to 9.5% from 14.0% in nine months, and restructuring will continue, with about USD 70.0 million of further charges expected through 2030.

### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

The asset base is being run for cash. Capital spending of USD 226.3 million in 2025 was 43.4% of depreciation and amortization of USD 521.6 million, and the 2026 outlook of about USD 200.0 million is 42.6% of the expected USD 470.0 million, so spending is held well below depreciation and its maintenance share is not stated. Over twelve months free cash flow was 61.4% of trailing reported EBITDA, but nine-month free cash flow was negative before the litigation payment is added back, so conversion depends on the fourth-quarter working-capital release. Cash interest of USD 170.2 million over twelve months absorbs 47.2% of trailing reported EBITDA.

### Porter's five forces

Rivalry is the force that matters most: Olin competes with large chlor alkali producers in North America and, in epoxy, with Huntsman, Westlake and Asian producers, and subsidised Asian exports are cited by management as a pressure on the fourth quarter, which transmits into lower prices and margins. New entrants are a weak force because plants need large capital investment and permits. Buyers are moderately strong: chlorine goes to a small number of industrial users and Winchester sells to retailers and governments. Suppliers matter for Winchester, which buys propellant mainly from one large supplier and metals at exchange-linked prices, and for energy, which is the largest raw material. Substitutes for chlorine and caustic soda are not established from the sources.
### Political, economic and regulatory factors

Regulatory and economic factors are material and social and technological factors are not. Environmental obligations carry a reserve of USD 156.8 million and expected expense of USD 25 million to USD 30 million in 2026, the State of Texas has sued over emissions at Freeport, and the clean hydrogen production tax credit that benefited chlor alkali results is smaller in 2026, with the annual pretax benefit expected at USD 15 million to USD 20 million to 2028. Trade policy is fluid after the 20 February 2026 Supreme Court ruling on emergency tariffs, Winchester reports partly tariff-driven metal inflation, and Middle East conflict has raised feedstock and energy costs, though the issuer reports no significant direct effect.
### SWOT in credit terms

Strengths are liquidity of USD 1,244.4 million, no maturity before November 2027, a backlog of USD 1,331 million and discretionary cash that has been cut. Weaknesses are reported leverage of 7.76x, cover of 2.12x, one-site and one-segment concentration and thin free cash flow. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a full recovery of the Freeport plant, cost actions and, if the documents bear it out, a merger that lowers combined leverage. Threats that could weaken it are covenant relief ending before earnings recover, a failed merger with a termination fee of USD 121 million, and a repeat outage.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

For the next twelve to 24 months the outlook is a weak fourth quarter, then a recovery that depends on chlor alkali, with merger closing expected in the first quarter of 2027, covenant relief ending by 30 September 2027 and the receivables financing due in November 2027. Tailwinds are stable domestic electrochemical unit values, structural cost actions, improving epoxy volumes and Winchester pricing; headwinds are weak global demand, subsidised Asian exports, higher feedstock and metal costs and planned turnarounds. Over three to five years restructuring charges continue to 2030, the hydrogen tax credit declines after 2028 and merger synergies are not quantified in the sources, so the medium-term earnings level is not established.

### Qualitative downside scenario

The downside begins with a second operating shock at Freeport or a prolonged weak chlor alkali price on top of year-end destocking. The first operational break is the vinyl chloride monomer plant running at reduced rates, as in the second quarter of 2026, when the issuer said the disruption reduced adjusted EBITDA by USD 40.0 million. That lowers trailing reported EBITDA to USD 320.8 million, lifts net leverage to 8.72x and cuts interest cover to 1.88x, and a failed merger with the USD 121 million termination fee would lift leverage to 9.10x on unchanged cash. Liquidity of USD 1,244.4 million still covers the USD 465.0 million receivables financing, so distress within a year is not indicated, but the covenant relief, under which no covenant limited borrowing at 30 September 2026, ends by 30 September 2027 and headroom after it is not calculable. Management can cut capital spending, guided at about USD 200.0 million for 2026, and the quarterly dividend of about USD 22.7 million, while asset sales are limited during relief. Observable triggers are fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA below USD 80 million and any slip in merger closing.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Olin presents a not fully assessable business profile supported by liquidity, a long maturity profile, improving epoxy and Winchester results and the absence of a sponsor, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 7.76x on reported EBITDA, thin free cash flow and concentration in chlor alkali at one site. Cash-flow durability appears weak at this earnings level because free cash flow after dividends is near break-even, depends on a fourth-quarter working-capital release and sits beside recurring add-backs. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on fourth-quarter earnings, the end of covenant relief by 30 September 2027, the receivables financing due in November 2027 and the merger terms. The primary downside path is a second outage or weak chlor alkali prices meeting the end of covenant relief before earnings recover. Further analysis would require the covenant levels, the merger agreement, Huntsman's statements and peer data, and the business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established. Fundamental credit analysis completed with limitations. Top risk: covenant relief ending before earnings recover.
